title: Measuring the impact of ChatGPT in enhancing number sense acquisition: A mixed-method study
extended_summary:
This study asks whether integrating ChatGPT into mathematics instruction improves junior high school students’ understanding of number concepts, and how students perceive the tool’s usefulness. The authors note debate over whether generative AI can meaningfully improve achievement in mathematics, especially for foundational number sense skills.

The intervention was a quasi-experimental classroom study combined with qualitative analysis. One 7th-grade class at Junior High School State 10 Manado used ChatGPT during seven 90-minute mathematics sessions, while a control class received conventional teaching. In the experimental condition, ChatGPT was used for explanations, question-answering, problem solving in pairs, and independent exercises. Quantitative data came from pre-test and post-test math scores, including both LOTS and HOTS items; qualitative data came from student essays about their experiences with ChatGPT.

The quantitative results showed significant pre-post gains within both the ChatGPT and control groups, but no significant difference between the two groups’ post-test performance. The effect sizes were small, indicating that ChatGPT did not directly improve measured mathematics achievement in number concepts. Qualitatively, however, students reported that ChatGPT increased efficiency, improved understanding, provided generally accurate help, and supported them when they were stuck. The paper concludes that ChatGPT is better viewed as a supplementary tool that may support learning processes and higher-order problem solving, rather than as a replacement for traditional instruction or a guaranteed driver of achievement gains.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental mixed-method study with a control group and pretest-posttest design, which provides moderate causal evidence but not full RCT rigor. Credibility is limited by the small sample, single school setting, and the reliance on qualitative perceptions for some claims.
impact_tier_rationale: The main academic outcome showed no significant benefit of ChatGPT on mathematics achievement (p=0.913), so overall impact is unclear to modest at best. There was a small within-group gain in the experimental class (d=0.265) and positive perceptions about efficiency, but not enough for a stronger impact rating.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT-supported mathematics learning for 7th-grade students, used by the teacher for additional explanations, by students for question-answering, problem solving, and independent अभ्यास on number concepts

finding.finding_summary: In a quasi-experimental mixed-method study with 7th-grade students (experimental n=39; control n=37), ChatGPT integration did not significantly improve number sense / number-concept achievement compared with conventional instruction. Post-test scores were not significantly different between groups (p=0.913), and the reported pretest-posttest effect within the experimental group was small (d=0.265).
finding.measure: Mathematics test scores on 20 multiple-choice items covering number concepts, including LOTS and HOTS questions; pretest and posttest; independent and paired t-tests

finding.finding_summary: Although the quantitative achievement results were null, the qualitative findings suggested ChatGPT supported higher-order thinking and problem solving, especially on HOTS items where scores increased from 12.820 to 18.590 in the experimental class. Students also reported improved understanding and easier handling of difficult problems, but these were perception-based findings rather than a direct standardized measure of critical thinking.
finding.measure: Descriptive performance on HOTS versus LOTS math items; student essays on perceived understanding/problem-solving support
finding.study_size: n=39 qualitative; n=39 experimental for HOTS/LOTS descriptives

finding.finding_summary: Students consistently reported that ChatGPT improved efficiency and speed in studying, helping them find answers quickly and complete exercises faster. This was a qualitative finding from 39 student essays, not a quantified productivity metric, but the direction of perceived effect was clearly positive.
finding.measure: Student perceived efficiency/speed in learning and task completion from open-ended essays
